_anchors.canvas.w: 48 = the size the arthropod grammar is authored at, and the Chrono-tier cell. This sample is the target.
_anchors.canvas.originY: canvas.h * 0.54, placing the thorax so antennae and feet both clear the frame at scale 1
_anchors.tones.perMaterial: 4, the opening conviction of BACKLOG round 1. Value separation, not tone count, is what this idiom bets on.
_anchors.frames.walk: 8, twice the control: two frames per named phase, which is what buys the anticipation the Chrono bar is set on. 5 was tried first and was wrong - with phases at 0, 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4, a 5-frame cycle shows exactly one of the four key poses and interpolates past the rest.
_anchors.light.x: unit vector from the upper left, held identical across all four probe samples
_anchors.light.curve: 1.8. Measured by looking: at 1.0 the lower-right half of the body was a single dark mass with the legs lost inside it.
_anchors.light.y: the y half of light.x's unit vector
_anchors.outline.enabled: on: selective darkening is the Chrono-tier reading of an outline
_anchors.outline.inner: on: value separation is the whole claim of this idiom, and the line between two touching parts is where value separation is decided
_anchors.outline.rim: off. The silhouette edge by value instead of line - a rim on the lit side, an occlusion edge on the shadow side. This is the knob the silhouette round is comparing against outline.enabled, and it is off in every sample that predates the round.
_anchors.body.scale: 1 = identity; the grammar is authored at this size
_anchors.gait.swing: 0.09 turn, from the 7 px femur: about 4 px of foot travel, the stride 48 px can carry
_anchors.gait.lift: 1.5 px = thorax height (2 * ry = 10) / 6.7, one eighth of the body at this scale
_anchors.texture.speckle: 0: the target idiom spends its budget on value separation, not on noise
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 75 ms. 8 frames x 75 = the shared 600 ms cycle.
_anchors.playback.scale: 4, because 48 x 4 = 192 px on screen, the shared cell size
_anchors.light.z: the lamp sits slightly on the viewer's side. Backfilled when the depth solver arrived: at -1 every surface faces the light and the body flattens to one tone, at 0 the light grazes and the far half goes black. -0.35 puts the centre of a mass around two thirds up its ramp and still leaves the lit and shadow edges at the two ends.
_anchors.gait.depth: canvas.w / 8 = 6 px. Backfilled with the depth solver; no track in this sample uses the z channel, so it is inert here. It is the body's half-width rather than 0 so that it already means something the day a depth track is added.
